changes.before: Implement validMinutes(value). Match the worked contract and the changed-input checks without modifying the supplied input values.
changes.after: Accept only whole-number minutes from 1 through 180.

before: A numeric field needs both a type rule and an allowed range. This contract accepts whole numbers from 1 through 180, including both endpoints.
This exercise is a small pure JavaScript model. Its inputs are supplied directly; it does not receive live HTTP requests, operate a database, or deploy a service.
Number.isInteger does not coerce text into a number. >= and <= include the endpoint values. && means all three conditions must pass.

Read the function call validMinutes(1) from the inside out: the arguments supply the inputs, validMinutes runs the body once, and return sends its result back to the caller. console.log displays that result; it does not change it.
Does the string "25" satisfy this numeric JSON-field contract? The contract accepts a number. A query-text parser would use a different, explicit conversion step.
after: A valid minutes value must meet two rules: it is a whole number, and it is from 1 through 180. Return true only when both rules pass.
Number.isInteger(value) checks for a number with no fractional part. It rejects fractions, text, and values such as NaN or Infinity.
value >= 1 allows 1 and larger numbers. value <= 180 allows 180 and smaller numbers. The && operators require all three checks to pass.
Text such as "25" is not the number 25. This check does not convert it. Reading numeric text from a query would require a separate, deliberate conversion step.
Complete validMinutes(value). Keep 1 and 180 valid. Reject fractions, numbers outside the range, and non-number inputs. Do not change the supplied value.
